newsitem.title: UK: UK's National Express in bus joint venture.
newsitem.headline: UK's National Express in bus joint venture.

text.p: Britain's National Express Group said on Monday it had formed a joint venture with Schoyen Group, one of Norway's largest bus operators.

The new company, to be named Concordia Bus, will be jointly owned 63 percent by National Express and 37 percent by Schoyen. It intends to tender for public transport contracts and acquire existing bus companies in the Nordic countries and Germany.

Frode Larsen, Schoyen president, will chair the joint venture while National Express chief exceutive Philip White will be deputy chairman. The board will comprise three further National Express directors and two from Schoyen.
Concordia will seek to capitalise on the experience of National Express in running bus operations and Schoyen's market intelligence and local presence.
Schoyen, a broadly based transport business, provides about 40 percent of Oslo's bus services and its bus division employs around 800 staff.
"The private sector is set to play an increasingly important role throughout Europe in the provision of public transport services," said National Express chief executive White.

"National Express' experience of operating in the highly competitive, deregulated UK transport sector combined with Schoyen's local expertise will make Concordia a powerful force in the Nordic countries and allow us to take advantage of the extensive opportunities in this region."
